ops.title: Transcript host budgets are 512 MiB facts and 1408 MiB retained since 12.92.8
ops.body:
Since capt-hook 12.92.8 (PR #352, commit bb12d1b06de9) the Go host handshakes the snapshot owner with `snapshots.HostConfig()`: 512 MiB of prepared facts (`max_prepared_fact_memory_bytes`) and 1408 MiB retained (`max_retained_bytes`), with the 512 MiB hook reserve unchanged. The embedded default stays 128 MiB / 1024 MiB; `HostConfig()` adds the 384 MiB difference to retention so snapshots keep the room they had.

Why 512: on 2026-10-10 the facts for one registry's 897 traces measured 337,067,415 accounted bytes, and the largest of 8,610 live cache entries was 1,727,664 bytes. A replay of 897 synthetic facts at that size (same binary and workload, config only) read 897 entries and 281,882,291 logical bytes on every foreground graph query at 128 MiB / 1024 MiB, and 0 at 512 MiB / 1408 MiB once warming finished, with the same answers. Cost in that replay: owner RSS 793 MB to 1,473 MB; retained peak while warming 906,929,458 bytes against a 939,524,096 background cap.

Limits of that evidence: synthetic facts, logical bytes rather than physical IO, a dev-profile build. Captain Hook has no resource-monitor memory cap, so the larger retained cap is bounded only by the store's own ledger.

Coupling: the change needs cc-transcript 14.40.0 (PR yasyf/cc-transcript#53), whose `usage` carries 20 counters including `prepared_cache_reads` and `prepared_cache_bytes_read`. The schemas here require all 20, so the pin is exact; release order is producer first, then pin, lock, and regenerated schemas.

How to check a live host: `capt-hookd version` and `status` for the build; `go version -m` on the installed `capt-hookd` for `vcs.revision`; a `stats` call through `captain_hook.snapshots.client.client_scope()` for the cumulative counters and gauges. No runtime surface echoes the handshake config itself, so the budgets are proven by build provenance plus `TestSnapshotServiceHandshakesTheHostBudgets`, not by a live read.
